summary: Verified heal-on-reconnect fix for the missed-image bug on BOTH sides. Backend REST endpoints used by the heal path (agent: GET /api/chat/sessions/{id}/messages, customer: GET /api/chat/public/{id}/messages?session_token=…) correctly return persisted messages+attachments. Frontend integration test proved the actual bug scenario: patched WebSocket via addInitScript to capture all sockets, forcefully closed the agent WS, then had a customer-side WS deliver 'HEAL_TEST_iter14_missed_msg'. The message was NOT in the agent UI immediately (as expected — WS was down), and after the useWebSocket 2-second reconnect backoff fired plus the heal-on-reconnect useEffect re-fetched via /api/chat/sessions/{id}/messages, the message appeared in the agent's chat view (within 1s of reconnect). Regressions verified: FRONTEND_TEST_MSG absent, no email-capture UI/testids/'Share your email' text, Real-time connected banner works, happy-path image upload+download (customer→agent via ?auth=<token>) still works.
critical_code_review_comments: AgentDashboard.jsx (924 lines) and ChatWidget.jsx (974 lines) both still exceed the 700-line guideline (carried over from iter12/iter13).

The heal-on-reconnect useEffect on AgentDashboard (lines 286-295) depends on the whole `sess` object; if useAgentSessions returns a new reference each render, `wasConnected.current = connected` will still be correct BUT sess.loadSessions() will fire on every reconnect. That's fine because it's idempotent, but a stable ref via useCallback in useAgentSessions would be cleaner.
useWebSocket 2s reconnect backoff has no jitter and no cap — on repeated failures the server could get hammered. Consider exponential backoff with jitter (low priority).
The heal effect on ChatWidget (line 338-346) uses raw fetch instead of the `api` axios instance; not a bug (endpoint is public and doesn't need Bearer), but inconsistent with the rest of the widget.
seed_data_creation: One anon session per test run with client_id prefix 'iter14_' / 'iter14ui_'. No cleanup required (they naturally age out and hold trivial data).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Playwright WS-drop technique: use page.add_init_script BEFORE page.reload() to install a wrapper around window.WebSocket that captures every socket into window.__sockets. Then window.__sockets.forEach(s=>s.close()) to simulate a network hiccup. The app auto-reconnects after 2s (see useWebSocket). Also note: outbound python-urllib/requests requests to the preview domain sometimes get CF 403 depending on UA — safer to use page.evaluate(async ()=>fetch(...)) from inside the browser context when the test lives inside a Playwright session. Backend login returns 'token' (not 'access_token').
